How tidal turbines survive winter

Published on 4 March 2026 by the engineering desk

Tidal turbines spend their working lives in one of the harshest environments an engineer can design for.

The machines sit on the seabed for months at a time. Storms churn sand across their blades, and the water never stops moving.

What actually fails

Bearings fail first in almost every recorded case. The seals that keep seawater away from them are the real design problem.

We stopped trying to keep the sea out and started designing for the day it gets in.

That change of mindset produced a generation of turbines that can be serviced at sea instead of being hauled back to a dry dock.
